name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic Dallas-area seat
Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised) and name recognition
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
Open seat removes incumbency but the underlying partisan baseline dominates
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean and a favorable national environment point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and Allred's fundraising and profile far exceed those of Republican Patrick Gillespie, who reports no fundraising. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic win, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any sign of Gillespie fundraising or outside Republican spending targeting the open seat would be the first signal of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves this Dallas-area seat open, but the district's strong Democratic lean of about 18 points makes it very difficult terrain for Republicans. Democrat Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee, enters with roughly $7.4 million raised and high name recognition, while Republican Patrick Gillespie shows no reported fundraising or outside support.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 95 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a Democratic margin in the low twenties. The seat remains safely Democratic despite the open-seat dynamic.
